analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and changelog changes: two new changelog.d fragments, a new build.md paragraph (head lines 27-31), and a new test.md section on provider authorization guidance. No Swift source, test code or workflow changes were supplied, so the described behavior cannot be verified from this batch.

The fragments describe two behavior changes in the provider CLI. Status and doctor now keep reporting App Attest authorization until the coordinator lease expires, instead of requiring a renewal within 10 seconds. Status and doctor also stop offering MDM removal unless the coordinator decision is fresh enough for removal readiness. `darkbloom unenroll` keeps its 10-second renewal requirement.

Both changes are consistent with TB-011 and its receipt/removal readiness language. In TB-011, MDM removal needs a fresh coordinator decision, and the basic lease is separate from receipt monitoring. In TB-002, a live App Attest grant is independent of legacy trust fields. The display change appears to be advisory only. The described CLI behavior does not extend serving authorization, proof age or lease lifetime, and it is more conservative about MDM-removal advice.

T-057, MDM removal advice and T-052 are the relevant threats. The stated design (removal advice requires a fresh decision, existing profiles stay installed) does not weaken those controls. Unchecked: whether the actual status/doctor code derives lease and freshness from authenticated coordinator state, and whether the 'unexpired lease' display uses a trusted clock. The Swift sources, including ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests, were not supplied. The next pass should check those code paths if they appear in another batch.

The docs claim the new tests cover the receipt-window boundary and exact lease expiry. That is documentation only, and no test evidence was reviewed.
